title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff ordering + regional queue thresholds
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: This hotfix addresses two related SLO enforcement regressions observed during a cross-region capacity event: (1) the regional circuit-breaker/backoff ordering could thrash when multiple regions began failing at near-similar times, causing repeated failovers and increased latency; and (2) the per-region request queue threshold was too conservative for our larger customers, triggering premature load shedding.

Motivation & context: During the incident on 2026-02-18 (internal postmortem linked in ENG-4652), we observed oscillation where the SLO enforcer would trigger backoff for region A, then immediately prefer region B, then flip back when region B started showing transient errors. The root cause was a non-deterministic ordering and an aggressive backoff reset path that did not account for in-flight re-routing. Separately, dedicated customers with sustained high throughput were experiencing load-shedding even though downstream capacity was still acceptable; the threshold was tuned for median workloads and needs to be larger for dedicated pools.

This PR makes the following changes (high level):
- Stabilize backoff ordering by introducing a deterministic region-preference tiebreaker and by smoothing backoff decay so ordering flips are less likely under transient noise.
- Increase per-region request queue thresholds for Dedicated and high-throughput Dedicated-preview customers, with config guarded behind a feature flag.
- Fix a race in the circuit-breaker state transition that allowed transient close->open transitions during reconfiguration.
- Add unit and integration tests that simulate concurrent failovers and verify no thrash for 30s under repeated transient errors.
- Add a small operational note to the SLO enforcer docs about the new feature-flag and how to tune thresholds.

Checklist:
- [x] Reproduce thrash locally and in staging
- [x] Unit + integration tests added
- [x] Feature flag for threshold increase (off by default in hosted)
- [x] Canary rollout plan described below
- [x] Monitoring/alerting adjustments included

Commits (summary):
- fix(slo/enforcer): deterministic region tiebreaker and backoff smoothing (A. Martinez)
- fix(slo/enforcer): circuit-breaker state machine race fix (A. Martinez)
- perf(slo/config): bump dedicated per-region queue thresholds behind feature flag (A. Martinez)
- test(slo): add concurrent-failover integration test (A. Martinez)
- docs(slo): document new feature flag and tuning guidance (A. Martinez)

Files changed (high level):
- src/slo/enforcer/core.rs -- backoff ordering and state-machine changes (60 additions, 28 deletions)
- src/slo/enforcer/circuit_breaker.rs -- race fix and additional guards (34 additions, 12 deletions)
- pkg/config/defaults.yaml -- increased default thresholds for dedicated (16 additions, 6 deletions)
- tests/integration/slo_failover_test.go -- new integration test harness (18 additions)
- docs/slo/enforcer.md -- operational notes and rollout steps (10 additions)
- deploy/flags/feature_flags.yaml -- feature flag gate for threshold change (4 additions)

Small illustrative diff snippets:
- src/slo/enforcer/core.rs: changed selection ordering to sort candidate regions by (healthy_score, deterministic_seed(region_id)) and added exponential decay smoothing to backoff windows.
- src/slo/enforcer/circuit_breaker.rs: added compare-and-swap around state transitions and a short debounce window when reconfig triggers are received.

Canary & rollout plan:
- Stage: deploy to staging and run the added integration test, verify no thrash for 10 minutes under synthetic load (completed in CI)
- Canary: roll out to Dedicated-preview customers first (feature flag off by default); monitor region failover rate, SLO-enforcer-trigger rate, and application 95p latency for 60 minutes.
- Gradual: if no regressions, enable feature flag for additional Dedicated customers across two weeks; keep automatic rollback in place if failover rate increases > 2x baseline.

Monitoring & alerts updated:
- Added slo_enforcer.backoff_flip_rate metric and alert when > 0.5 flips/min for > 5m in canary scope
- Added dedicated.queue_oom_rate alert suppressed for flag-enabled clusters until thresholds converge

Notes on risk and mitigation: The change includes a feature flag and conservative threshold bump to limit risk to hosted customers. Circuit-breaker race fix is low-risk (locks/debounces only during transitions) and covered by unit tests. Canary will exercise real traffic patterns before wider rollout.

Related: ENG-4652 (postmortem), ENG-4720 (customer bug report), SUP-2984 (support ticket).

review_comments: Liam Chen: Can you explain how the deterministic tiebreaker interacts with the smart-routing policies? We should avoid making region preference too sticky.

Ava Martinez: The tiebreaker only applies when healthy_score is equal within a small epsilon. It uses a deterministic hash of region_id combined with a short-lived epoch to avoid stickiness longer than the backoff decay window.
Priya Kapoor: Please add a unit test covering the CAS path for the CB transition (requested change).
Ava Martinez: Added unit test and increased debounce from 50ms to 200ms to be conservative; test included in latest commit.
Noah Patel: CI flaky test observed in integration run — re-run CI after squashing commits. Approved after green CI.
